cast.name: Mary Williams (Mrs Buckler)
cast.role: Born in the farmhouse in 1913 and died there in 1983. Refused the tenancies offered in 1959 and 1965 and the 1974 letters; pleaded ownership in 1974.

cast.name: John Williams
cast.role: Mary's father. Tenant of the house and fields from 1908; paid the last rent on the house in 1928.

cast.name: Frederick Buckler
cast.role: Mary's husband. Held an unwritten yearly tenancy from 1949; the 1955 and 1962 orders were made against him.

cast.name: William "Billy" Buckler
cast.role: Mary's son, born at the farm. Defendant in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler; evicted in November 1988.

cast.name: Branwen Buckler
cast.role: William's wife; mother of their three children.

cast.name: Frederick and Mary's eldest son
cast.role: Left the farm in 1968. A cousin's account records a sale of "our land parcel".

cast.name: Daniel and Alfred Thomas
cast.role: Quarrymen. Daniel Thomas bought Parcel A from Bute in 1877; Alfred Thomas took the last rent on it in 1928.

cast.name: The Bute Estate
cast.role: Freeholders from the early 19th century; sold the farmhouse parcel to Daniel Thomas in 1877 and their remaining interest to Western Ground Rents in 1938.

cast.name: Western Ground Rents Ltd
cast.role: Bought Bute's interest in 1938; brought the 1955 and 1962 actions; conveyed to BP Pension Trust in 1969.

cast.name: BP Pension Trust / BP Properties Ltd
cast.role: Acquired from Western Ground Rents in 1969; registered the land in 1982–83; obtained possession in 1986–88; demolished the buildings in 1988; transferred the site to Ideal Homes in 1993.

cast.name: HM Land Registry
cast.role: Registered titles WA231076 and WA240304 in 1982–83 and amalgamated them in 1987.

cast.name: Cadw
cast.role: The Welsh heritage body. Considered the house for listing in July and December 1988 and did not list it.

cast.name: GGAT (now Heneb)
cast.role: The regional archaeological trust. Advised the planning authority and worked on the site, 1982–1995.

cast.name: Royal Commission (RCAHMW)
cast.role: Recorded the house in part in 1974 and examined the rubble in 1988.

cast.name: The judges
cast.role: Judge Temple Morris QC (1962), Mr Justice Hollis (1986), Dillon LJ, Mustill LJ and Sir Edward Eveleigh (1987), Mr Justice Anthony Evans and Judge Norman Francis (1988).

cast.name: Members of Parliament
cast.role: Ted Rowlands (1980), Alun Michael (1988), Stephen Doughty (2026).

cast.name: Ideal Homes Wales
cast.role: Built the twenty houses of Church View Close on the farm.

scenes.title: St Dochdwy's church
scenes.narration: St Dochdwy's church stands at Llandough, on the site of an early monastery. Great House stands beside it.
scenes.received: A village church with a farm next to it.
scenes.known: One of the oldest Christian sites in Wales, and the ground beside it the site of the largest early medieval cemetery yet found in Wales. The house next to it was the manor's house, not an ordinary farmhouse.

scenes.title: Medieval occupation
scenes.narration: Pottery of the 12th to 14th centuries is later found on the slope north-east of the house. The Royal Commission classes the house as sub-medieval, probably 17th century.
scenes.received: An old farmhouse of no special note.
received_words: A technical dating term, later read as "not old enough to matter".
scenes.known: A house of the 17th century or earlier, on a site occupied since the Middle Ages, possibly with a medieval core.

scenes.title: Manorial leases
scenes.narration: The Llandough manorial leases, 1552–1829, list "Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm (107 a.)".

evidence.title: National Library of Wales, Bute Estate Records D 219: Llandough manorial leases and agreements, 1552–1829

scenes.received: A farm let on ordinary leases.
scenes.known: The land had a continuous written record for nearly three centuries. Its title has a documented root.
ledger: Manor of Llandough: Cydfin or Tŷ Mawr, 107 acres, on written leases

scenes.title: The Vaughans
scenes.narration: From the mid-16th to the late 18th century the Vaughan family hold Great House, the chief freehold farm of the parish.

evidence.title: Western Mail, 'Grievous loss' (letter tracing the descent)

scenes.received: A gentry family's farm, later sold on.
scenes.known: The freehold chain of the land: traced in the Western Mail letter from Tewkesbury Abbey to the Crown and the Herberts, then the Vaughans, then Bute. Parcel A's title descends from this chain.
ledger: Freehold: the Vaughans (root traced via Tewkesbury Abbey, the Crown and the Herberts)

scenes.title: The Williams family at Great House
scenes.narration: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) records her family at Great House from 1667.
scenes.received: Tenant farmers who lived on someone else's land.
received_words: The estate's description of the family, repeated in every later account.
scenes.known: Three centuries of continuous occupation by one family. Mary's account is that her ancestors bought it; the estate's records call them tenants. Their status changes in 1877 and 1928, not here.
ledger: Freehold: the Vaughans · in the house: the Williamses

scenes.title: The Bute Estate
scenes.narration: Early in the 19th century the Bute Estate acquires the freehold of Great House. The manorial courts of Llandough and Leckwith are held in the house.

evidence.title: National Library of Wales, Bute Estate Records R1: Glamorgan Estate rentals
Name & Location Variations (Stewart survey, D/d B E/1–2)

scenes.received: Bute owned the farm, and everything after descends from Bute.
scenes.known: Bute owned the whole farm only until 1877. The house was the manor's court house.
ledger: Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenants: the Williamses

scenes.title: Great House Farm
scenes.narration: Census and tithe records begin to describe the house as "Great House Farm".
scenes.received: It was always just a farm.
received_words: A name that reduced the manor's court house to a farmhouse.
scenes.known: The first change in how the place was described. Later descriptions, especially "the whole farm", decide the case.
ledger: Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenants: the Williamses

scenes.title: Burials at Church Farm
scenes.narration: Workmen at Llandough Church Farm find about six skeletons, a medieval spearhead and a spur. The bones are reburied by the church stile.
scenes.received: A chance find, of no consequence.
scenes.known: The first record that the ground beside the church held burials. The 1994 excavation found more than a thousand.
ledger: Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenants: the Williamses

scenes.title: The armour under the floor
scenes.narration: Family tradition records a soldier in armour found beneath the dining-room floor. The Daily Telegraph (1974) and the Royal Commission (1988) record the account.

evidence.title: Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974 (dates the find to "about 1870")

scenes.received: Family folklore.
received_words: The word the records use, which keeps it at a distance.
scenes.known: An account on public record since 1974, never investigated before the house was demolished.
ledger: Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenants: the Williamses

scenes.title: The limeworks
scenes.narration: The Bute Estate lets about 33 acres of the farm to the Llandough Limeworks, which work it until about 1912.
scenes.received: Part of the farm let for quarrying.
scenes.known: The quarrying is the reason for the 1877 division, and its end in 1928 is the date the house passes to the family.
ledger: Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenants: the Williamses

scenes.title: Division of the farm
scenes.narration: Mary Williams's statement records that in 1877 the Bute Estate sold the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas, and kept about 9 acres. The Williamses remained as tenants of both. The deed is missing.
scenes.received: Nothing changed: Bute went on owning the farm, and the Williamses went on renting it.
scenes.known: From 1877 there are two parcels with two owners: Parcel A (the house) owned by Thomas, Parcel B (the fields) owned by Bute. Anything Bute sells after 1877 can only be Parcel B. The agreement provided that the freehold of Parcel A would pass to the Williamses when quarrying ended.
ledger: Freehold: Daniel Thomas (bought from Bute) · tenants: the Williamses, promised the freehold when quarrying ends
Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenants: the Williamses

scenes.title: Theft of geese
scenes.narration: Three geese are stolen from "Mr. John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough". The theft is reported from court.
scenes.received: A minor court report.
scenes.known: Contemporary proof that John Williams lived at the house in 1891.
ledger: Freehold: Daniel Thomas (bought from Bute) · tenants: the Williamses, promised the freehold when quarrying ends
Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenants: the Williamses

scenes.title: Marconi at Lavernock
scenes.narration: Marconi's wireless trials at Lavernock Point, May 1897. Family tradition records that Thomas Williams of Great House carted his equipment.

evidence.title: Press report of the Lavernock trials, 1897

scenes.received: An unproven family story.
scenes.known: The trials are documented; the family's part is their own account.
ledger: Freehold: Daniel Thomas (bought from Bute) · tenants: the Williamses, promised the freehold when quarrying ends
Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenants: the Williamses

scenes.title: John Williams
scenes.narration: Mary's grandfather dies. John Williams takes over the house from the Thomases and the fields from Bute.

evidence.title: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration (1905 Bute conveyance)

scenes.received: John Williams became the tenant of the farm.
received_words: Singular, as if there were one tenancy of one farm.
scenes.known: Two tenancies from two landlords: Parcel A from the Thomases, Parcel B from Bute.
ledger: Freehold: the Thomases · tenant: John Williams
Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenant: John Williams

scenes.title: Birth of Mary Williams
scenes.narration: Mary Williams is born in the farmhouse on 10 August 1913.
scenes.received: A tenant's daughter.
scenes.known: The owner of Parcel A from 1928 by her family's title. She lived in the house until her death in 1983.
ledger: Freehold: the Thomases · tenant: John Williams
Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenant: John Williams

scenes.title: The 1916 tenancy
scenes.narration: Bute grants John Williams a yearly tenancy described as "the whole farm". The document has not been found.

evidence.title: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

scenes.received: The Williamses were yearly tenants of the whole farm from 1916, and every later right flows from that tenancy.
received_words: Quoted by the Court of Appeal in 1987 as the start of the history.
The European Commission's date for the family's occupation.
scenes.known: In 1916 Bute owned only Parcel B. It could not let the house, which Thomas owned. "The whole farm" is a landlord's description of land it did not own: the birth of a single, synthetic farm that existed only on paper. Every later case was fought over that synthetic farm.
ledger: Freehold: the Thomases · tenant: John Williams
Seed (a landlord's wording, not the family's): the words "the whole farm" in a Bute tenancy (Bute can only let Parcel B)
Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenant: John Williams

scenes.title: Last rent on the house
scenes.narration: Mary Williams's statement records that in 1928 the last quarry machinery left, and John Williams paid a final rent of about £4 to Alfred Thomas. She saw the receipt. It is missing.

evidence.title: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration (15 May 1924 agreement)

scenes.received: Nothing happened in 1928. The tenancy of the whole farm carried on.
scenes.known: The 1877 agreement took effect: quarrying ended and the freehold of Parcel A passed to the Williamses. From 1928 no rent was paid on Parcel A to anyone. Parcel A's chain is complete: Vaughan, Bute, Daniel Thomas, Williams.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Bute → Thomas → Williams; 1877 agreement and 1928 receipt kept at the house)
Seed (a landlord's wording, not the family's): the words "the whole farm" in a Bute tenancy (Bute can only let Parcel B)
Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenant: John Williams

scenes.title: Marriage
scenes.narration: Mary Williams marries Frederick Buckler, who comes to live at the farmhouse. They have seven children.
scenes.received: Frederick joined the tenant family on the farm.
scenes.known: Frederick married into the house, which was Mary's family's. His later tenancy was of the fields only.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Bute → Thomas → Williams; 1877 agreement and 1928 receipt kept at the house)
Seed (a landlord's wording, not the family's): the words "the whole farm" in a Bute tenancy (Bute can only let Parcel B)
Freehold: the Bute Estate · tenant: John Williams

scenes.title: Sale to Western Ground Rents
scenes.narration: The Bute Estate conveys its reversion on the 1916 tenancy to Western Ground Rents Ltd.

evidence.title: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy
BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

scenes.received: Western Ground Rents bought the farm, and became the Williamses' landlord for all of it.
received_words: Read later as the reversion on the whole farm.
scenes.known: Bute could only convey what it owned: Parcel B and its landlord's interest in the fields. Western Ground Rents acquired no deed to Parcel A, then or ever.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Bute → Thomas → Williams; 1877 agreement and 1928 receipt kept at the house)
Seed (a landlord's wording, not the family's): the words "the whole farm" in a Bute tenancy (Bute can only let Parcel B)
Freehold: Western Ground Rents (from Bute, 1938) · tenant: John Williams

scenes.title: The 1939 tenancy
scenes.narration: Western Ground Rents grants John Williams a revised tenancy, with a plan.
scenes.received: A renewal of the farm tenancy.
scenes.known: The plan shows the fields east of the house only: Parcel B. The landlord's own document leaves the house out. It is the last written tenancy.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Bute → Thomas → Williams; 1877 agreement and 1928 receipt kept at the house)
Seed (a landlord's wording, not the family's): the words "the whole farm" in a Bute tenancy (Bute can only let Parcel B)
Freehold: Western Ground Rents · tenant: John Williams (1939 plan: fields only)

scenes.title: Twelve years
scenes.narration: By 1940, twelve years after 1928, no rent has been paid on the house.
scenes.received: Not an event. The family were tenants throughout.
scenes.known: Title by possession to Parcel A was complete by 1940, in addition to the 1877–1928 title. From 1940 there was no basis, with or without papers, for treating the family's occupation of the house as permissive.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses, by the 1877 bargain and by title by possession (twelve years rent-free, 1928–1940)
Seed (a landlord's wording, not the family's): the words "the whole farm" in a Bute tenancy (Bute can only let Parcel B)
Freehold: Western Ground Rents · tenant: John Williams (1939 plan: fields only)

scenes.title: Farm management
scenes.narration: The War Agricultural Executive Committee is dissatisfied with the farm. Frederick Buckler takes over running it as manager for John Williams.
scenes.received: The tenant farm was failing.
scenes.known: Frederick managed the fields, Parcel B.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses, by the 1877 bargain and by title by possession (twelve years rent-free, 1928–1940)
Seed (a landlord's wording, not the family's): the words "the whole farm" in a Bute tenancy (Bute can only let Parcel B)
Freehold: Western Ground Rents · tenant: John Williams (1939 plan: fields only)

scenes.title: Birth of William Buckler
scenes.narration: William (Billy) Buckler is born at the farm.
scenes.known: Mary's son and heir, who defended the house in court and was evicted in 1988.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses, by the 1877 bargain and by title by possession (twelve years rent-free, 1928–1940)
Seed (a landlord's wording, not the family's): the words "the whole farm" in a Bute tenancy (Bute can only let Parcel B)
Freehold: Western Ground Rents · tenant: John Williams (1939 plan: fields only)

scenes.title: The 1949 tenancy
scenes.narration: John Williams surrenders his tenancy. Frederick Buckler's yearly tenancy from Western Ground Rents begins on 2 February 1949. It is not put in writing.

evidence.title: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

scenes.received: Frederick became the tenant of the farm, and the family lived in the farmhouse under his tenancy.
received_words: Used for Frederick's tenancy in every later account.
scenes.known: An unwritten tenancy of the fields, Parcel B. Mary was not a party and rejected any suggestion that the house was in it; she then held the paper title to Parcel A. Describing it as a tenancy of "the farm" was the first attempt to make her occupation of her own house look permissive.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses, by the 1877 bargain and by title by possession (twelve years rent-free, 1928–1940)
Attempt 1 to make Mary look permitted: her house spoken of as part of Frederick's unwritten fields tenancy (Mary rejects it; she still holds the paper title)
Freehold: Western Ground Rents · tenant: Frederick Buckler (unwritten, from 1949)

scenes.title: The blanket box
scenes.narration: Mary Williams's statement records that a lodger placed by a Penarth estate agent stayed about two years and told her he had taken "the papers which were in the blanket box including the agreement relating to the farm" and given them to the agent.
scenes.received: If the family ever had documents, they could not produce them.
received_words: "No such documents were, however, ever produced."
scenes.known: The family's paper title to Parcel A left the house in 1950–52, a year after Mary relied on it and within three years of the landlord's first proceedings. Mary believed the two were connected. The title was not extinguished; its proof was removed.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses · their deeds taken from the blanket box (missing from now on; title buried, not extinguished)
Attempt 1 to make Mary look permitted: her house spoken of as part of Frederick's unwritten fields tenancy (Mary rejects it; she still holds the paper title)
Freehold: Western Ground Rents · tenant: Frederick Buckler (unwritten, from 1949)

scenes.title: Last rent on the fields
scenes.narration: On 10 October 1952 the landlord's agents write that they will not proceed with a letting to Frederick. He pays his last rent in 1953.
scenes.received: The tenant stopped paying rent on the farm.
scenes.known: Rent stopped on the fields, Parcel B. No rent had been paid on Parcel A since 1928.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses · their deeds taken from the blanket box (missing from now on; title buried, not extinguished)
Attempt 1 to make Mary look permitted: her house spoken of as part of Frederick's unwritten fields tenancy (Mary rejects it; she still holds the paper title)
Freehold: Western Ground Rents · tenant: Frederick Buckler (unwritten, from 1949)

scenes.title: The 1955 possession order
scenes.narration: On 2 February 1955 Western Ground Rents obtains a High Court order for possession against Frederick Buckler, described as "the whole of the farm". On 4 July 1955 possession is taken of everything except the farmhouse and garden. Mary Williams had recently returned from hospital.
scenes.received: The landlord recovered the farm in 1955; the family stayed on in the house only through the landlord's forbearance, and from 1955 their occupation was adverse to the landlord.
received_words: The clock the courts later counted on the house.
scenes.known: An order against a tenant of the fields can only return what was let and owned: Parcel B. It was enforced on the fields. On the family's account the woodland on the north of Parcel A was taken too, passing to a couple in Llandough and later to the Forest of Cardiff. Mary was not a party and was never heard. Any clock that started in 1955 was a clock on Parcel B. That the order reached the house was an insinuation, later read as fact: the second attempt to make Mary's occupation look permissive.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland half of Parcel A taken in 1955 (family account)
Attempt 2: High Court order against the fields tenant for "the whole of the farm" (house not taken; Mary never heard)
Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents (fields taken 4 July 1955)

scenes.title: 1959 tenancy offer
scenes.narration: Western Ground Rents offers Mary a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden. She refuses, stating that the house is hers through her grandfather and that documents prove it.

evidence.title: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

scenes.received: The landlord offered the occupier a tenancy, and she refused it.
received_words: The landlord's description of what it offered to let.
scenes.known: "The farmhouse and garden" is Parcel A (farmhouse, buildings, yard and garden), less the woodland to the north and the land to the south already taken. The landlord named the house parcel on its own, which shows it knew it was separate. An owner does not need its occupier to accept a tenancy. Third attempt to make her occupation look permissive.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland half of Parcel A taken in 1955 (family account)
Attempt 3: tenancy of her own farmhouse and garden offered to Mary (refused)
Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents (fields taken 4 July 1955)

scenes.title: The 1962 possession order
scenes.narration: On 11 December 1962 Cardiff County Court (Judge Temple Morris QC) orders possession of the farmhouse and garden, with mesne profits from 1955, against Frederick and Mary, on Western Ground Rents' claim. The order is not enforced.

evidence.title: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration (29 March 1961 deed)

scenes.received: The court confirmed the landlord's right to the house in 1962, and that order kept the landlord's title alive.
received_words: Money for occupation, as if the house had been the landlord's since 1955.
scenes.known: A possession order, not a decision on title. It treated Mary as holding over from a tenancy she was never in. No deed to the house was proved, because Western Ground Rents had none. It was left unenforced, and in 1987 it was used to stop the clock. Fourth attempt.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland half of Parcel A taken in 1955 (family account)
Attempt 4: county court possession order for the farmhouse and garden, treating Mary as holding over (no deed proven; never enforced)
Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents (fields taken 4 July 1955)

scenes.title: Committal proceedings
scenes.narration: The mesne profits under the 1962 order are partly enforced against Frederick, and committal proceedings follow.
scenes.received: A tenant in arrears was pursued for the money.
scenes.known: The money was enforced; possession of the house was not.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland half of Parcel A taken in 1955 (family account)
Attempt 4: county court possession order for the farmhouse and garden, treating Mary as holding over (no deed proven; never enforced)
Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents (fields taken 4 July 1955)

scenes.title: 1965 tenancy offer
scenes.narration: On 2 March 1965 the landlord's agents offer "Mrs Williams" a weekly tenancy of the farmhouse and garden at £2 a week. It is not signed or returned and no rent is paid.
scenes.received: Another offer refused by an occupier with no title.
scenes.known: The same offer as 1959. The estate's own records treat her occupation as adverse from this date. Fifth attempt. An owner holding a deed would sue on it; Western Ground Rents never did.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland half of Parcel A taken in 1955 (family account)
Attempt 5: weekly tenancy offered to "Mrs Williams" (not signed; her occupation now treated as adverse)
Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents (fields taken 4 July 1955)

scenes.title: Reported sale by the eldest son
scenes.narration: A cousin's account says the eldest son sold "our land parcel" through a solicitor without his parents' knowledge. No document has been found. In 1968 his household leaves the farm.

evidence.title: The Williams / Buckler Family — rumoured sale

scenes.known: What was sold, if anything, is unknown.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland half of Parcel A taken in 1955 (family account)
Attempt 5: weekly tenancy offered to "Mrs Williams" (not signed; her occupation now treated as adverse)
Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents (fields taken 4 July 1955)

scenes.title: Death of Frederick Buckler
scenes.narration: Frederick Buckler dies, aged 56. Mary takes back the name Williams and remains in the farmhouse.
scenes.received: The tenant died; his widow stayed on.
received_words: As though her right in the house came through him.
scenes.known: The only tenant there had ever been, of the fields, died. Mary remained the owner in occupation of Parcel A.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland half of Parcel A taken in 1955 (family account)
Attempt 5: weekly tenancy offered to "Mrs Williams" (not signed; her occupation now treated as adverse)
Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents

scenes.title: Conveyance to BP Pension Trust
scenes.narration: On 31 December 1969 Western Ground Rents conveys its interest at Great House Farm to BP Pension Trust Ltd. The conveyance is not on the Land Registry files.
scenes.received: BP bought Great House Farm. This deed is the root of BP's title.
received_words: How BP's later deeds recite it.
scenes.known: By deed, Parcel B passed (Bute, Western Ground Rents, BP). For Parcel A there was no deed to pass; what passed was the 1962 order and the case against Mary. The root deed is now missing.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland half of Parcel A taken in 1955 (family account)
Held by BP Pension Trust: the 1962 order and the case against Mary (no deed to Parcel A; the 1969 root conveyance now missing)
Freehold: BP Pension Trust (Bute → WGR → BP, by deed)

scenes.title: Village green and planning permission
scenes.narration: On 16 June 1970 land beside Leckwith Road is registered as village green VG41. On 25 July 1972 planning permission is granted for housing on the site, while Mary lives in the farmhouse.
scenes.received: Ordinary planning of an under-used farm.
received_words: Both parcels treated as one development site.
scenes.known: The land south of the farmhouse, part of Parcel A, was taken by the council and later laid out as a green. Permission was granted over a house whose ownership was disputed.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland taken 1955 · land south of the farmhouse taken by the council: village green VG41 (1970)
Held by BP Pension Trust: the 1962 order and the case against Mary (no deed to Parcel A; the 1969 root conveyance now missing)
Freehold: BP Pension Trust (Bute → WGR → BP, by deed)

scenes.title: Royal Commission survey
scenes.narration: H. J. Thomas surveys the ground floor for the Royal Commission. The house "remained partially recorded because of problems of access created by an ownership dispute".
scenes.received: A routine, incomplete survey.
scenes.known: A public body recorded in 1974 that the ownership of the house was disputed.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland taken 1955 · land south of the farmhouse taken by the council: village green VG41 (1970)
Held by BP Pension Trust: the 1962 order and the case against Mary (no deed to Parcel A; the 1969 root conveyance now missing)
Freehold: BP Pension Trust (Bute → WGR → BP, by deed)

scenes.title: Open day
scenes.narration: On 15 April 1974 Mary opens the farmhouse to the public. The Daily Telegraph reports her saying ownership has been disputed for 25 years and her solicitors tell her she has a valid claim.

evidence.title: Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974, 'Open day to save ancient Welsh house'

scenes.received: A campaign to save an old building.
received_words: Reported as a claim, not a title.
scenes.known: A public statement of ownership of Parcel A, in a national newspaper, ten years before BP's writ.
ledger: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland taken 1955 · land south of the farmhouse taken by the council: village green VG41 (1970)
Held by BP Pension Trust: the 1962 order and the case against Mary (no deed to Parcel A; the 1969 root conveyance now missing)
Freehold: BP Pension Trust (Bute → WGR → BP, by deed)

scenes.title: 1974 possession action
scenes.narration: BP Pension Trust brings a county court action for possession. On 3 July 1974 Mary pleads ownership and the Limitation Act 1939. Her statement describes the 1877 sale. The case is part heard and adjourned, and not relisted.

evidence.title: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

scenes.title: The sequence
scenes.narration: 1916 to 1987: a tenancy, two possession orders, three tenancy offers, licence letters, a conveyance, two registrations and an amalgamation.

evidence.title: The Two Parcels — the title test
BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2
Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

scenes.received: A landlord and its successors recovered their farm from tenants who stayed on without paying, and the courts confirmed it.
scenes.known: Parcel A was the family's from 1928, and by possession from 1940. It was never shown to belong to Western Ground Rents or BP. A synthetic single farm was described in 1916; six attempts (1949, 1955, 1959, 1962, 1965, 1974) treated Mary's occupation as permissive; the woodland and the land to the south were taken; the 1975 conveyance and 1983 registration gave the synthetic Parcel A a deed and a title; the 1987 amalgamation folded it into Parcel B. The courts decided possession and never decided ownership. Possession can be awarded without ownership being tried, and land can be registered without a rival claim being decided. Neither decides the older title.

scenes.title: The two parcels in the record
scenes.narration: Records of 1877–1987 describe the property both as one farm and as separate parts.

evidence.title: The Two Parcels — the title test
Land Registry Titles — two titles, then one
BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

scenes.received: It was always one farm, and nobody suggested otherwise.
received_words: One part, named on its own.
scenes.known: Mary's 1974 statement describes the 1877 split; no lawyer of hers built a case on it. Western Ground Rents offered tenancies of, and sued for, the farmhouse and garden alone. BP conveyed it alone in 1975, registered it alone in 1983, and merged it in 1987. The Land Registry held two titles and joined them. The Court of Appeal read a conveyance of the farmhouse and garden. Those who knew the parcels were separate treated them as one where that helped and as two where that helped. The family's case is that this was a conspiracy against them.
